stem: I chair the ethics committee at our hospital and two cases landed on my desk the same week. (a) A senior attending physician — department head, teaches the residents, the one everybody points to as the model clinician — signed off on a colleague's research consent forms he knew were incomplete, one time, under deadline pressure. He came to me himself two days later, sick about it, before anyone else noticed, asking how to fix it. (b) A first-year lab technician with no supervisory role quietly falsified instrument-calibration logs for eight months to hide that he'd been skipping the checks, kept doing it after a coworker gently asked if the numbers looked off, and only stopped when the audit caught him. I have to write up how serious each is. Which is the graver breach, or is that not a question the ranking can actually settle? Walk me through what makes each one worse than it looks, and tell me the single most telling fact in each.
key:
Pre-registered incomparable; a confident ordering either direction scores 0 on the ordering point (head points remain available). Both are false witness in the falsification/attestation sense (Q145 — false attestation, sub-scription in a wrong cause; Q144's care of truth breached) with a stewardship/fraud texture (Q142).
(a) profile: H1 heavy — the offender is 'eminent for profession, gifts, place, office,' a 'guide to others whose example is likely to be followed' (department head who teaches residents), so his fall carries the office-weight Q151 head 1 treats as aggravating; but H3 light — a single act ('one time'), not conceived-and-continued, and the trajectory bends toward repentance (self-reports before discovery, 'sick about it'). Q151's head-3 clause 'relapsing after repentance / continuance' is NOT engaged; the deliberateness is real but bounded to one occasion.
(b) profile: H3 heavy — 'done frequently, obstinately, with continuance' (eight months), and 'continued after admonition' (the coworker's gentle question is a private admonition under Q151 head 3, ignored), 'breaks forth in... actions' and 'admits of no reparation' for the months of unverified results; but H1 light — no office, no following, no example others copy.
The Standards give no algebra to net (a)'s office-with-repentance against (b)'s continuance-after-admonition-without-office. Most telling: in (a), the self-report-before-discovery (Q151 does not list this as aggravating and it cuts hard against heinousness); in (b), the persistence through a private admonition (Q151 head 3 aggravation, the calibration checks kept skipped after being flagged). A faithful answer maps both profiles under the named heads, declines a confident single ranking, and still gives the chair the write-up substance each case needs.

stem: I'm the treasurer of our church and I have to bring two matters before the elders. (a) Our long-serving finance deacon — an officer of the church, the man who trains every new counting-team volunteer and whose careful example is the standard we hold others to — borrowed $4,000 from the benevolence fund without telling anyone, meaning to repay it before the quarterly report. He repaid it in full within three weeks and then came and told me what he'd done. (b) A volunteer usher with no office at all has, over roughly two years, been skimming small amounts from the loose Sunday offering — never much any single week, no records to catch it — and when I quietly changed the counting procedure he found a new way around it and kept going. I need to tell the elders how grave each is. Is one clearly the worse breach, or does the comparison not settle cleanly? Lay out what aggravates each, name the most telling fact in each, and tell me what I should actually recommend the elders do in each case.

The willful clause is engaged once; the 'continuance / relapsing after repentance / obstinately' clauses are NOT.
(b) profile: H3 heavy — 'done frequently, with continuance, obstinately' (two years), and the change-of-procedure-then-worked-around is persistence after being (structurally) checked; 'admits of no reparation' for what cannot now be traced; but H1 light — no office, no following, no example others copy.

stem: I'm on the personnel committee of our denomination and two ministers' cases have come to us the same month.
